title: docs: two MCP tool descriptions and 13 daemon code comments still say the daemon never runs git
description: Follow-up from qa-7100be29's review of task-16aac8b4 (DONE, d09ef1e). That task fixed CLAUDE.md and docs/**/*.md and added daemonGitDocs.test.ts, but it was docs-only, so the claim survives in code. The daemon's one git call is the read-only `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch` fingerprint in util/diskState.ts. It never writes git state, lands, pushes or runs the gate. Two MCP tool descriptions still say "never runs git": recordCandidate.ts:39 and recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:41. Agents read these in tools/list, so they matter most. The same phrase is in 13 code comments: policy.ts, providerDescriptor.ts, candidateStore.ts, receiptStore.ts, finalizeAttempt.ts and schema.ts (x4). The full list is comment-f724b231 on task-16aac8b4. The epic-3d096d59 rail uses the same phrase; that rail belongs to the human and is out of scope here.
definitionOfDone: recordCandidate.ts and recordDeliveryReceipt.ts tool descriptions and the 13 listed comments use the ARCHITECTURE.md Delivery Path wording (never writes git state, lands, pushes or runs the gate; one read-only status fingerprint)
daemonGitDocs.test.ts (or a sibling) also asserts that no registered tool description claims the daemon never runs git, and it fails on today's two descriptions
npx tsc --noEmit and the daemon suite pass

implementationPlan.description:
REWORD THE 13 LINES in the ARCHITECTURE.md 'Delivery Path' vocabulary: the daemon never writes git state, lands, pushes or runs the gate; it never checks what a runner reported against git; its one git call is the read-only `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch` handoff fingerprint in util/diskState.ts. Every rewrite must stay TRUE in its own context. Most of these lines are about verification, so the true statement there is 'never checks X against git', not a blanket negation.

The two MCP descriptions, which agents read in tools/list, get exact text:
- tools/recordCandidate.ts:39: 'The daemon never runs git: the shas are recorded as reported and checked for shape (7-40 hex) only.' becomes 'The daemon never checks these shas against git: they are recorded as reported and checked for shape (7-40 hex) only.'
- tools/recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:41: 'The daemon never runs git and verifies nothing about the target: a receipt is a reported landing, not proof.' becomes 'The daemon never reads the target ref or checks this report against git: a receipt is a reported landing, not proof.'

The 11 comments get the same treatment, fitted to context:
- recordCandidate.ts:29, recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:17, candidateStore.ts:19, receiptStore.ts:12, finalizeAttempt.ts:26, policy.ts:26, and schema.ts:539, :625, :1024 and :1154. For each, say which reported value is never checked against git, or that the daemon never writes git state or lands or pushes, whichever the sentence is about.
- providers/providerDescriptor.ts:8 ('does not launch agents and never runs git, and it MUST NOT start doing either') becomes 'does not launch agents or write git state (its one git call is a read-only status fingerprint), and it MUST NOT start doing either'.

Keep each hunk to its sentence. MCP tool contracts are unchanged: only prose moves. The epic-3d096d59 rail stays out of scope; it belongs to its human owner.

GREEN: `npx vitest run src/util/daemonGitDocs.test.ts` = 4 passed (4). All 13 lines reworded with the built-in Edit tool (TOOL-tier attribution; EOL kept: 7 LF files 0 CR, schema.ts CR=LF=1354). Every hunk stays inside its own sentence.
- recordCandidate.ts:39 uses the plan's exact text.
- providerDescriptor.ts:8 uses the plan's text, reflowed across 4 lines.
- The rest say which reported value is never checked against git: policy.ts (gate + records), candidateStore.ts (baseRevision/treeSha), receiptStore.ts (receipt), finalizeAttempt.ts, recordCandidate.ts:29 (shas), recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:17 (report), schema.ts:539 (commit sha), :625 (attested artifact/PR), :1024 (candidate shas), :1154 (receipt).
DEVIATION 1, recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:41: I did NOT use the plan's 'never reads the target ref or checks this report against git'. The fingerprint (diskState.ts, `# branch.oid`) reads HEAD, and HEAD is normally the checked-out consolidation branch the wrapper lands on (deliveryTarget = refs/heads/<branch>). So 'never reads the target ref' is literally false in the same way 'never runs git' was. I used the minimal true edit instead: 'The daemon never checks this report against git and verifies nothing about the target: ...'.
DEVIATION 2, same reason: the same sentences also said 'reads no ref' (recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:17), 'inspects no ref' (receiptStore.ts:13) and 'inspects the target' (schema.ts:1155). Each became 'checks the report/receipt against git'.
MCP contract unchanged: only description prose changed. Peers' dirty paths (skillFiles.ts, startStep.ts, contextNextAction.ts, recommendSkill*.ts, docs/skills, .moe/*) untouched.

comments.content:
SELF-REVIEW (step-4, worker-3c030e77)

1. Truth in context. None of the 13 rewrites says the daemon never touches git. Each is scoped to what the sentence is about:
- policy.ts:26: never runs the gate or checks records against git.
- providerDescriptor.ts:8: does not launch agents or write git state; it names the one read-only status fingerprint.
- candidateStore.ts:19: baseRevision and treeSha are never checked against git.
- receiptStore.ts:12: performs no landing and never checks a receipt against git.
- finalizeAttempt.ts:26: never checks a report against git.
- recordCandidate.ts:29: the handler never starts a process or checks the shas against git.
- recordCandidate.ts:39: the plan's exact text.
- recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:17: never checks the report against git.
- recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:41: never checks this report against git and verifies nothing about the target.
- schema.ts:539 (the commit sha), :625 (the attested artifact or PR), :1024 (the candidate shas) and :1154 (the receipt report): each is never checked against git.
DEVIATION from the plan's :41 text 'never reads the target ref': diskState.ts's `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` reads HEAD (`# branch.oid`). HEAD is normally the checked-out consolidation branch, which is the delivery target (deliveryTarget = refs/heads/<branch>). So 'never reads the target ref' is literally false in the same way 'never runs git' was. The same sentences also said 'reads no ref' (recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:17), 'inspects no ref' (receiptStore.ts:13) and 'inspects the target' (schema.ts:1155); each became 'checks ... against git'.
SIBLINGS FOUND IN REVIEW, now fixed (+1 path): recordDeliveryReceipt.ts:56 and :60 inputSchema property descriptions (targetBefore/targetAfter), which agents read, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md:853, all said 'the daemon never reads the ref' / 'reads no ref'. They now say 'never checks it/a receipt against git'. `git grep -niE "reads no ref|never reads (the|a|any) (target )?ref|inspects no ref"` over docs, CLAUDE.md and non-test daemon src is now empty. This keeps the plan's aim that this is the last sweep of this claim.

2. MCP contract unchanged. Only prose changed: record_candidate's description, and record_delivery_receipt's description plus two property descriptions. Tool names, parameters, types, required lists and refusal codes are untouched. No test pins the old text (grep checked). tsc --noEmit exits 0.

3. Scan breadth.
- It deliberately skips receiptStore.test.ts:218 and :641 ('never touches git or a process: no child process in the store/tool'); both are TRUE of the unit they test.
- Mutation proofs in a HEAD export:
  - Empty walk (filter -> false) turns the source test RED.
  - Non-recursive walk turns it RED; all 4 arrayContaining entries live in subdirectories.
  - Empty registry turns the tools test RED.
  - The inputSchema half: with the phrase injected into record_candidate.taskId's property description, the tools test goes RED with ['moe.record_candidate']. It stays green once the JSON.stringify(inputSchema) clause is removed, so that clause is what catches it.
- Known ceilings:
  - The scan is per line, so a wrapped phrase slips through (existing ponytail comment).
  - It matches only the regex family, so sibling phrasings such as 'reads no ref' are fixed but not guarded.
  - A TRUE sentence about another component ('the proxy never runs git') would trip it. The failure message says what to write instead.

4. Diff and EOL.
- git diff --stat shows 10 paths: the 9 planned plus docs/MCP_SERVER.md, +94/-33. Peers' dirty paths are untouched.
- EOLs are kept: the 8 LF sources, MCP_SERVER.md and the test all have 0 CR. schema.ts is CR=LF=1354 (was 1353; one wrapped line added).
